components.name: Display Module (OLED)
components.reasoning: This component includes both the screen itself as well as related electronics like touch sensors, and forms the primary user interface. It's distinct due to its specialized manufacturing process and typically procured as a complete assembly from dedicated suppliers.

components.name: Battery Pack (Li-ion)
components.reasoning: The battery module provides essential rechargeable power capacity and must be charged regularly for device functionality. It is universally included in smartphones as a separate, distinct unit with its own supply chain and management system.

components.name: Main Circuit Board (PCB)
components.reasoning: This encompasses the core processor, memory, and various other critical chips essential to a smartphone's computing capabilities. The PCB is integral yet often sourced independently from specialist manufacturers rather than fabricated internally by OEMs.

components.name: Camera Module
components.reasoning: Integrated high-resolution imaging systems are crucial for photography and video recording features in most smartphones today, frequently assembled as discrete components with dedicated optics and image processing chips.

components.name: Chassis/Frame (metal or ceramic)
components.reasoning: The chassis provides structural support essential for design integrity and serves critical roles including durability and integration of various subassemblies. While sometimes integral to other parts, it's often specified independently to allow different material choices impacting the device.

components.name: Speakers (stereo or single channel)
components.reasoning: High-quality internal speakers are essential components enabling clear communication and multimedia playback functionalities in smartphones. They're typically sourced separately for easy customization of speaker size, quality, and acoustics.

components.name: Vibration Motor
components.reasoning: Used primarily to provide haptic feedback during device operation, such as notification alerts or screen selection responses; it's commonly bought from specialized suppliers but may be optional in some models due to market preferences.

components.name: Antenna Module (RF)
components.reasoning: Ensures wireless connectivity across multiple frequencies necessary for mobile network communication protocols (4G, 5G, Wi-Fi). These usually come from specialized suppliers and must meet stringent performance standards.

components.name: Power Management ICs (PMIC)
components.reasoning: Specialized circuitry regulating various aspects of power delivery within the phone including charging, discharging, and voltage regulation across multiple systems, commonly sourced from dedicated semiconductor vendors.

components.name: Touch Controller IC
components.reasoning: Critical for interpreting user input on touch screens enabling basic interaction, typically integrated though still distinguishable as a separate component by suppliers specializing in human interface devices.

components.name: Wireless Charging Coil
components.reasoning: An increasingly common feature allowing for contactless charging, often provided by a specific supplier but not universally included in all smartphone designs due to varying market preferences and cost considerations.

components.name: Flash Memory (EMMC/NAND)
components.reasoning: Provides internal storage space for OS, apps, and user data, essential non-volatile memory typically procured as discrete units from semiconductor manufacturers like Samsung or Micron to meet performance standards.

components.name: Wireless Connectivity Chips (Wi-Fi/Bluetooth)
components.reasoning: Enables wireless communication features vital in smartphones including internet connectivity via Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for file transfers, connections with other devices, etc., commonly sourced separately from specialized IC manufacturers.
